newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer sees 96 operating profit up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bayer sees 96 operating profit up 10 pct.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG said on Tuesday that it was confident it will meet its 1996 sales target of 47 billion marks ($31.1 billion) and post an operating profit increase of 10 percent.
"Based on the figures so far this year, we are confident of meeting our full-year target of 47 billion marks," Bayer said in a letter to shareholders.

Additionally the group said, "we continue to assume that operating income will be up 10 percent." At the same time however Bayer said that it expects additional charges in the fourth quarter due to early retirements and other factors.
Bayer also announced an 18 percent rise in group net profit to 2.3 billion marks in the first nine months of the year.
Group pre-tax profit in the first nine months rose by 12 percent to 3.7 billion marks from 3.3 billion.
The pre-tax profit was broadly in line with analysts' expectations which had ranged from 3.68 billion marks to 3.78 billion.
Group sales were up 7.4 percent at 36.5 billion marks, also within expectations.
The company's shares were down 10 pfennigs or 0.2 percent at 57.30 marks in pre-bourse electronic trade after the results.
In the third quarter, pre-tax profit totalled 981 million marks, up 8.3 percent year-on-year, Bayer said.
